Private AI · The Command Core

Stop renting your intelligence. Own it.

Every prompt your team types goes to someone else's servers. Every seat is a bill that never ends. Private AI puts your own AI on your own equipment, set up around your business. We choose it. We deploy it. We run it. You own it.

Apply for the Command Core↗See what it costs ↓

By Phila Ngwenya · Checked against sources 29 September 2026

Your week, on rented AI

You already use AI. You just don't own any of it.

Look at your team's week. Someone pastes a client contract into a chat window to summarise it. Someone else drafts a proposal on a personal account. It's quicker. So they do it.

Where did that contract go? To a server you've never seen. In a country you didn't choose. Under terms nobody read.

78%

of people using AI at work were bringing their own tools. That was 2024. Is your team different?

Source: Microsoft & LinkedIn Work Trend Index, 2024 ↗

Your best information is leaving the building. One paste at a time.

Put a number on it

What is renting really costing you?

Take one AI seat. What does it cost you a month? Now times your headcount. Now times 12.

Next year you do it again, with more people. The bill never stops. And at the end of it, you own nothing.

Then there's the cost you won't see on an invoice.

Under POPIA section 72, sending personal information to a company in another country needs adequate protection or the person's consent. Every client file pasted into a foreign AI tool is one of those transfers. Who signed off on it?

Source: POPIA, section 72 ↗

Renting is fine for a year. Not for your company's brain.

The usual fixes

Why banning it, buying seats or building it yourself doesn't work.

01

Ban it.

People use it anyway, on their phones. Now you have all the risk and none of the control.

02

Buy enterprise seats.

Better terms. Same problem. Your data still leaves, and the bill still grows with every hire.

03

Build it yourself.

Running your own AI takes people who look after the equipment, update the models and check the answers. Most firms don't have that team. Without it, the system slowly gets worse.

You don't need a data science department. You need someone to be one for you.

The fix

Your own AI. Run for you.

Private AI means the AI runs on equipment inside your business. Not ours. Not a tech giant's. Yours. We choose the equipment that fits. We set it up on your documents and build agents for your work. Then we keep it running.

Your data stays in the building.

Contracts, client files and numbers never go to an outside AI company. POPIA gets simpler, not scarier.

The cost stops climbing.

You pay to set it up and to run it. Not per person. Your next hire uses it without a new seat.

It knows your business.

It's set up on your templates, your past work and the way you write. So it starts every task already knowing you.

Free guide

If this sounds like you, get the AI Implementation Guide. It's the method we start every client on, free.

This isn't a fringe idea

The market is already moving this way.

$15.5 billion
Harvey, the legal AI company, raised $550 million at a $15.5 billion valuation. Their stated mission? To help legal teams own their intelligence.Source: Harvey, September 2026 ↗
1.7%
The quality gap has almost closed. Open-weight models, the kind you can run yourself, went from 8% behind the closed ones to 1.7% in a single year.Source: Stanford HAI, AI Index 2025 ↗
20 times faster
Altana, a supply chain company, built its AI on open models and its own private data. It now trains and deploys models more than 20 times faster, with 20–50% better performance. Not our client. Reported by Databricks.Source: Databricks customer story: Altana ↗

What it costs, honestly

Rent or buy? Here's the maths.

Owning costs more on day one. Renting costs more every day after that. So when does owning win?

A 2025 study by Pan and colleagues worked it out for firms running their own AI.

Time for owning to pay for itself, against renting

  • Small set-upswithin 3 months
  • Medium set-upsabout 4 to 34 months
  • The largest set-upsup to 69 months
Source: Pan et al., cost-benefit study, 2025 ↗

Where do you land? It depends on how much your team uses it. That's what your audit works out, before you commit to any equipment.

You don't guess. You see the numbers first.

When it's the wrong call

When private AI isn't for you. Yet.

  • Your files are a mess.

    AI is only as good as what you feed it. If your documents are scattered and out of date, we fix that first. It takes time. We'll tell you how much.

  • You want a creative all-rounder.

    For open-ended brainstorming, the biggest rented models still have an edge. Private AI wins on your own documents and your own processes.

  • Your team barely uses AI yet.

    Start smaller. Our corporate training gets them using it on their real work first. See the training →

I'd rather lose a sale than sell you the wrong thing.

Questions

What owners ask first.

What is private AI?+
It's AI that runs on equipment inside your business, not on someone else's servers. We choose the equipment, set it up on your documents and build agents for your work. Then we keep it running. You own it.
Is it as good as ChatGPT?+
For your own work, it's close enough that the gap stops mattering. Stanford's 2025 AI Index found open-weight models went from 8% behind the closed ones to 1.7% in a single year. For open-ended brainstorming, the biggest rented models still have an edge. We'll tell you straight which one your work needs.
Where does our data go?+
It stays with you. Your AI runs on your own equipment, so your documents aren't sent to an outside AI company. Before anything goes in, we agree in writing who can reach the system, and how.
What equipment do we need?+
You don't buy anything yourself. We choose the equipment that fits your team and your work. We deploy it and we look after it. The details come in your proposal.
Do we need our own IT team to run it?+
No. Running your own AI takes people who look after the equipment, update the models and check the answers. That's the part we do. It's the job most firms can't staff.
What does it cost?+
It depends on your team and how much you'll use it. Your audit works out the set-up cost and when owning beats renting for you. Engagements are limited, so apply first and we'll tell you if it's a fit.
Is this the same as the Command Core?+
Yes. Private AI is what the Command Core runs on. The Command Core is the whole engagement: the audit, your own AI, your agents and your team trained to use it.
